title: Triple Corn Orecchiette Carbonara with Guanciale
steps: Cheese and eggs: Grate the cheese and beat together with the 3 egg yolks until smooth.
Render guanciale: Place the guanciale in a cold pan and set over low heat. Cook gently Until the guanciale is crisp anc fat has rendered.
Reserve fat: Strain about 80% of the hot guanciale fat into the cheese-and-egg mix and beat again until it becomes a smooth, glossy emulsion. Set the crispy guanciale pieces aside.

Toast corn and frazzle chilli: Turn the heat up on the pan with the remaining fat. Toast one third of the corn kernels in the residual fat until lightly caramelized. Briefly frazzle the sliced jalapeño in the pan, then remove from heat.

Cook pasta with corn stem: Lightly salt boiling water. Add the reserved corn stem to infuse the pasta water, then drop in the orecchiette. Place the remaining corn kernels in a small sieve over the pasta (or cook them separately) and boil for 2-3 minutes.

Make corn cream: Take a small ladleful of pasta water and add it to a third of the cooked kernels; blitz until smooth to form a corn cream. Beat this corn cream through the egg-and-cheese mixture to integrate and loosen the sauce.

Combine and finish: When the pasta is al dente, add it to the toasted corn and marjoram in the pan, along with the remaining kernels. Remove the pan from direct heat and add the cheesy corn mix. Toss everything together until the sauce coats the orecchiette and looks rich and glossy. Fold in the crispy guanciales.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Carbonara is one of the most popular Italian pasta recipes. This particular one is a fusion version.

title: Pho Bo: Vietnamese Beef Noodle Soup
description: Pho is a classic Vietnamese noodle soup, supposedly invented in Hanoi in the early 20th century. With this dish, everything's about the broth—if you don't have the right broth, you don't have the dish.

ingredients.raw: 2 pounds oxtails, cut in 2- to 3-inch pieces
1 ounce light brown palm sugar, or 2 tablespoon light brown sugar
12 ounces beef top round, thinly sliced
1 bunch Scallions, thinly sliced, about 1 cup
Jalapeño chiles, stemmed and thinly sliced into rings

steps: For the beef stock: Preheat the oven to 350 F. Bring a large pot of water to a boil; add the oxtails, neck bones, and shank bones. Return the water to a boil and cook for 3 minutes. Drain into colander and rinse the bones thoroughly under cold running water. Rinse the pot and return the oxtails, neck bones, and shank bones to the pot. Add water, slowly bring to a simmer, and cook for at least 6 hours. Meanwhile, roast the onion and ginger on a rimmed baking sheet for 40 minutes.

Add the roasted onion and ginger to the simmering stock, along with the cinnamon, star anise, clove, cardamom pod, pepper, and palm sugar. Add the beef brisket and cook for 30-45 minutes; remove and allow the stock to continue to simmer, skimming off any scum that rises to the top. After 6-8 hours, remove pot from the heat and use a slotted spoon to discard the large solids. Strain the stock into soup pot through a fine-mesh sieve. (Note: To store, let cool completely; then transfer to airtight containers and refrigerate for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 3 months. Makes 6 quarts.)

For the soup: Thinly slice the top round and use the back of your knife to tenderize the meat slices; set aside. Slice the cooked brisket against the grain in thin slices; set aside. Blanch the bean sprouts in hot water; set aside. Season the stock with a few pinches of salt and fish sauce to taste.

Warm a serving bowl in hot water. Place the dried rice noodles in fine-mesh sieve; submerge the sieve in hot water and gently stir with tongs, 5–10 seconds. Place the cooked noodles in the warmed serving bowl. Top with brisket; then add a few slices of the top round and some chopped scallions and cilantro. Ladle the hot broth into the bowl, being careful not to submerge the top round. Serve immediately, accompanied by optional garnishes.

cultural relevance.reasoning: National, and international, comfort dish.

title: The Best Buttermilk Pancakes
description: We're transporting you to the old-fashioned diner for a plate of fluffy buttermilk pancakes.

ingredients.raw: 1 stick unsalted butter, melted and cooled, plus more for brushing
Butter and maple syrup, for serving
Butter and maple syrup, for serving

steps: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl. Whisk the eggs, buttermilk, vanilla and melted butter in a medium bowl until incorporated. Whisk the egg mixture into the flour mixture until just combined (it's OK if there are a few lumps).

Heat a griddle or large nonstick skillet over medium heat; lightly brush with butter. Pour 1/2 cup batter onto the griddle for each pancake and cook until bubbles form on top and the bottom is lightly browned, about 3 minutes. (If the pancakes are browning too quickly, reduce the heat to medium-low.) Flip and continue cooking until golden on the other side, about 1 more minute. Transfer to a plate. Repeat with the remaining batter, brushing the pan with more butter as necessary. Serve with butter and syrup.

cultural relevance.reasoning: A classic American breakfast item.

title: Vanilla No-Bake Cheesecake With a Chocolate Cookie Crust

ingredients.raw: 9 oz. (255 g) crispy chocolate cookies, such as Nabisco chocolate wafers (crust)
7 Tbsp. (99 g) unsalted butter, melted and cooled slightly (crust)
16 oz. (453 g) cream cheese, at room temperature (filling)
One 14-oz. can (397 g) sweetened condensed milk (filling)

steps: Grease a 9" springform pan with cooking spray or softened butter. Line the bottom and sides with parchment paper.

To make the crust, process the cookies, sugar, and salt in the bowl of a food processor until the cookies are finely ground. Pour in the butter and vanilla and process until the mixture holds together when squeezed. Alternatively, you may place the dry ingredients in a sealed resealable plastic bag, cover it with a tea towel, and crush the crackers with a rolling pin. Transfer the crumbs to a medium bowl and stir in the melted butter and vanilla. Scrape the crust mixture into the prepared pan and firmly press it into the bottom and 1" up the sides, using your fingers. Place the crust in the freezer while you make the filling.

To make the filling, briefly beat the cream cheese on medium-low speed in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, just until smooth, scraping the bowl with a flexible spatula as needed. Beat in the sweetened condensed milk and salt just until combined, and then the lemon juice and vanilla. Turn off the mixer as soon as all the ingredients are incorporated. Do not overmix or the cream cheese will lose structure. Scrape the filling into the prepared crust, smoothing the top with an offset spatula or butter knife. Cover the cheesecake with plastic wrap and refrigerate it for at least 5 hours, but preferably overnight.

When ready to serve, remove the sides of the pan and, if you would like to remove the base (though you don't have to), slide a long, serrated knife between the crust and the parchment paper and transfer the cake to a serving plate. Slice the cake with a large chef's knife that's been dipped in hot water and dried in between slices. Serve with a dusting of cocoa powder (if using). Keep the cake, wrapped, in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.

cultural relevance.reasoning: In the 1920s, Arnold Reuben (a Geman-Jewish immigrant in New York) popularized using cream cheese as the primary base and a graham cracker crust.

title: Spaghetti Napolitan (Japanese Ketchup Pasta)
description: Spaghetti Napolitan is a ketchup-based pasta and one of the popular yōshoku (Western-style food) dishes.

ingredients.raw: 60g / 2.1oz onion sliced into 1cm / ⅜" wide pieces

steps: Cook the pasta in a large pot of boiling water until al dente, following the packet directions.
Scoop out about a tablespoon of the cooking water, then drain the pasta.
Combine the sauce ingredients in a bowl and mix well.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Sauté the garlic and onion for about 1 1/2 to 2 minutes, until the onion turns translucent.
Add the capsicum, mushrooms, and ham, and sauté for about 1 minute.
Push the ingredients to one side of the pan and pour the sauce into the cleared space so it starts to bubble.
Stir the sauce for about 30 seconds to mellow its acidity, then combine it with the other ingredients.
Add the drained pasta and the reserved cooking water and toss quickly.
Add the butter and toss until it melts and coats the pasta, then turn off the heat.
Plate the pasta and serve with grated parmesan and Tabasco on the side.

cultural relevance.reasoning: It became an iconic menu item in traditional Japanese coffeehouses (kissaten) and family diners across the country.

title: Kheer (Simple, Homestyle Recipe)
description: A creamy Indian rice pudding made with rice, milk, sugar, cardamom, nuts, and optional rose water.

ingredients.raw: 1/3 cup rice 65 grams, I used basmati rice
1 teaspoon ghee also known as clarified butter
4-5 tablespoons sugar 50-62.5 grams, adjust to taste
3 tablespoons chopped nuts I used chopped cashews & almonds

steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then soak it in water and drain.
Heat a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat. Add the ghee, the drained rice, and the crushed cardamom and stir for 1 to 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the milk, stir, and raise the heat to medium-high. Bring the milk to a boil, about 10 to 12 minutes, stirring often so it doesn't stick.
Reduce to low heat and simmer for about 25 minutes, stirring every couple of minutes, until the rice is fully cooked and the mixture has thickened.
Stir in the sugar and chopped nuts and cook 5 to 10 more minutes, until the sugar dissolves. The kheer will thicken further as it cools.
Remove from heat and stir in the rose water, if using. Garnish with nuts and serve warm or chilled.

cultural relevance.reasoning: It is considered an auspicious dish and is frequently prepared as prasad (a sacred food offering) in Hindu temples and during major festivals like Diwali, Holi, and Raksha Bandhan. In Muslim households across South Asia, a closely related version called Sheer Khurma is essential during Eid celebrations.

title: Shredded Beef with Ancho Chile
description: Meal prep you'll actually crave: 8 servings with 50 g of protein each, and beef so tender it falls apart on its own. A smoky, thick sauce full of flavor, served with creamy mashed potatoes. It's also amazing with rice or tortillas. And it tastes even better reheated!

ingredients.raw: 2 dried morita chiles (if you want it spicy)

steps: Salt and pepper the beef and sear it in a hot pan with a little oil. Transfer it to your slow cooker or Instant Pot.

In the same pan where you seared the beef, add 1 sliced red onion, oregano, pepper, garlic powder, minced garlic, the tomato paste and the chiles (seeded and deveined). Add the chicken bouillon and 500 ml of the beef broth. Cook until the chiles soften.
Then take it out and blend everything together.
Pour this marinade over the seared beef. Add the rest of the beef broth and cook on low for 3 to 8 hours. Enjoy!

cultural relevance.reasoning: Carne deshebrada, barbacoa, o birria is a cornersone of mexican mestizo culinary heritage.

title: Shredded Beef Shepherd's Pie
description: Comfort food doesn't get much better than this. Fall-apart tender chuck roast, slow-braised in rich beef bone broth with hearty vegetables, all tucked underneath a golden layer of buttery mashed potatoes.

ingredients.raw: 3 lb chuck roast (for the shredded beef filling)
2 cups beef bone broth @kettleandfire (for the shredded beef filling)
1 large yellow onion, diced (for the shredded beef filling)
3 carrots, diced (for the shredded beef filling)
1 cup frozen peas (for the shredded beef filling)
3 cloves garlic, minced (for the shredded beef filling)
2 tbsp tomato paste (for the shredded beef filling)
1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce (for the shredded beef filling)
1 tsp fresh thyme (or 1/2 tsp dried) (for the shredded beef filling)
1/2 cup red wine (for the shredded beef filling)
1 tsp rosemary (for the shredded beef filling)
Salt & black pepper (for the shredded beef filling)
Salt & black pepper (for the shredded beef filling)
1 tbsp olive oil (for the shredded beef filling)
1-2 Tbs Flour (for the shredded beef filling)
3 lb Yukon Gold potatoes (peeled) (for the mashed potato topping)
4 tbsp butter (for the mashed potato topping)
1/2 - 2 cups warm milk (your desired thickness) (for the mashed potato topping)
Salt & pepper to taste (for the mashed potato topping)
Salt & pepper to taste (for the mashed potato topping)
2 Egg Yolks @peteandgerrys (for the mashed potato topping)
Grated Parm (for the mashed potato topping)

steps: Sear the beef: Season the chuck roast generously with salt and pepper. Rub on flour to coat the surface. Heat the olive oil in a Dutch oven and sear on all sides until deeply browned.

Slow braise: Add the onions, garlic, tomato paste, wine, Worcestershire, thyme, rosemary and beef bone broth. Cover and cook at 375°F in the oven for 3-4 hours, or until the beef easily shreds with a fork.

Make the filling: Shred the beef directly into its juices. (I removed the oil on the top.) Add the carrots and simmer until tender, then stir in the peas. If the filling is too liquidy, simmer uncovered until thickened or add a little bit of flour.
Make the mashed potatoes: Boil the peeled potatoes until fork-tender. Drain and run them through a potato ricer, then mix with the butter, warm milk, salt and pepper, Parmesan and egg yolks.

Assemble: Transfer the shredded beef filling to a baking dish and spread the mashed potatoes evenly over the top. Use a fork to create little ridges for those crispy golden edges. Grate more Parmesan on top.
Bake at 400°F for 20-25 minutes until bubbling and golden. Broil for the last 2-3 minutes for an extra crispy top!
Let rest for 10-15 minutes before serving. A little tip: don't rush the chuck roast! Low and slow is what turns an inexpensive cut of beef into the most tender, flavorful filling.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Shepherd's pie was a symbol of frugality in British households. Traditionally made with lamb or mutton.

title: Brown Butter Banana Bread Oatmeal Cookies
description: I made these completely by accident and they came out to be one of the best things I have ever made.

ingredients.raw: 1 very ripe banana, mashed, about 1/2 cup
Optional but VERY good: 1/2 cup chopped walnuts or pecans

steps: Brown the butter: Melt the butter over medium heat. Keep cooking and swirling until it foams, the milk solids turn golden brown, and it smells super nutty. Immediately pour it into a mixing bowl, including all those brown bits. Let cool for about 10 minutes.
Make the wet mixture: Whisk the coconut sugar into the brown butter. Add the mashed banana, egg yolk, and vanilla and whisk until glossy.
Add the dry ingredients: Stir together the whole wheat flour, oats, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt. Fold into the banana mixture just until combined. Fold in the nuts/chocolate if using.
Chill: This part matters because banana adds a ton of moisture. Chill the dough for 30-45 minutes.
Scoop: Heat the oven to 350°F. Scoop roughly 2-tablespoon portions onto a parchment-lined baking sheet. Keep them fairly tall rather than flattening them completely.

Bake: Bake for about 10-13 minutes, until the edges are set and golden but the centers still look slightly soft. Let them sit on the pan for 10 minutes. That's when the centers settle into that soft banana-bread texture.

title: Green Goddess Antioxidant Soup
description: This soup is absolutely packed with nutrients from broccoli, spinach, peas, leeks, onion and garlic. You're getting vitamins A, C and K, folate, potassium, fiber and antioxidants that help support immune function, skin health, digestion and overall cellular health. The chicken bone broth adds protein and minerals, while all those greens make this one of those meals that genuinely feels like you're giving your body something good.

ingredients.raw: 4 cups chicken bone broth (as always I only use @kettleandfire)
1/4 cup cream or milk (drizzle on top) (creamy finish)

steps: Sauté the onion, leek and garlic until soft. Add the potato, broccoli and bone broth. Simmer for 20-25 minutes until everything is tender.
Add the spinach and half the peas, then blend until completely smooth.
In a small pan, melt the butter, whisk in the flour, then slowly whisk in the cream until thickened. Stir half of it into the soup along with the remaining whole peas.
Season with salt and pepper and finish with a little drizzle of the rest of the cream.

cultural relevance.reasoning: The Green Goddess salad dressing originated in the Palace Hotel in San Francisco. In this case, it's used as a soup base.

title: Steak, Avocado and Cucumber Bowl
steps: Sear sirloin on each side for two minutes on high heat.
Put in the oven for 5 minutes at 400° then let rest for 5 minutes.
Dice all the other ingredients and add to bowl while steak cooks.
Add chopped up steak to bowl.
Add dressing and mix!

title: Caesar Dressing
steps: Mash the garlic with a fork until it turns into a paste. Then do the same for the anchovies, mix.
Add the yolk, mix. Add dijon, mix.
Constantly mixing, add the olive oil little by little; it should emulsify the mix.
Add the lemon zest and juice and the Worcestershire sauce. Mix.
Add pepper, mix. Add the grated parmesan, mix.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Originally from Tijuana, Mexico. Created by an italian chef. Culinary staple across the world.

title: Easy Yogurt Bagels with Savory and Sweet Spreads
description: EASY version bagels!! I'm using @fage Greek yogurt, which is my favorite, and the best part is that it provides 25 g of protein in a 250 g serving of yogurt.

ingredients.raw: Salt and pepper to taste (savory spread)
Salt and pepper to taste (savory spread)

steps: Add all the ingredients to the bowl of a stand mixer and mix until they start to come together into a dough.
Continue mixing with your hands, pressing and kneading until you form a smooth, even ball of dough.
Divide the dough into 6 equal portions and form a ball with each portion.
Shape the bagels: on a floured surface, roll each portion into a rope and join the ends, moistening them lightly with water to help them stick.
Place the bagels on a tray lined with parchment paper, flatten them slightly and brush with beaten egg.
Sprinkle with the seasoning, leaving some without.
Bake at 190°C for 25 minutes, or until the bagels are puffed and lightly golden.
Let rest for a few minutes before serving. Cut in half and toast.
To make the spreads, mix all the ingredients and season to taste.
Serve with cucumber, sliced tomato, capers, halved lemons, smoked salmon, chopped fresh dill, chopped walnuts and sliced banana.

cultural relevance.reasoning: In Eastern Europe bagels were served both to celebrate new life and to comfort mourners at shivah meals. This is now a New York-adapted bagel version.

title: Creamy Tuscan Salmon
description: Creamy Tuscan salmon, an all-time favorite recipe of mine that I love all year round, but especially in cozy season!

ingredients.raw: 3 or 4 fresh salmon fillets (season with salt, pepper, garlic, and paprika)
3 or 4 fresh salmon fillets (season with salt, pepper, garlic, and paprika)
3 or 4 fresh salmon fillets (season with salt, pepper, garlic, and paprika)
3 or 4 fresh salmon fillets (season with salt, pepper, garlic, and paprika)
3 or 4 fresh salmon fillets (season with salt, pepper, garlic, and paprika)
1 cup full fat coconut milk, canned
1 tsp arrowroot starch (or tapioca or cornstarch)
water, equal parts to the starch (from the steps)
drizzle of olive oil for cooking

steps: Season your salmon fillets with salt, pepper, granulated garlic, and paprika until each piece is coated.

Heat about a tablespoon of olive oil in a skillet pan to medium heat. Once sizzling, add your salmon fillets skin side up for 2-3 minutes. Flip and cook the other side for 3 more minutes. Remove from the pan and set aside.

For the sauce: in that same pan, add the diced onion and tomatoes and cook until softened. Then, add the minced garlic. Once the garlic is aromatic, add in the broth, coconut milk, and all seasonings.

While simmering, add arrowroot starch (or tapioca or cornstarch) to a small ramekin with equal parts water. Quickly mix to avoid clumping to make a slurry for the sauce. Add the slurry into the sauce. From here it should begin to thicken and the flavors should begin to incorporate. Add in the chopped spinach and basil.
Lastly, nestle the salmon fillets back into the sauce and cook for a few more minutes or until salmon is cooked internally to your liking. Enjoy!

cultural relevance.reasoning: Despite its name, Tuscan salmon is a modern Italian-American fusion dish rather than a traditional recope from Tuscany.

title: Grilled Scallops With Lemony Salsa Verde

ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, plus more for grilling
12 large sea scallops, side muscle removed

steps: Prepare grill for medium-high heat; oil grate. Toss scallops with 2 tablespoons oil on a baking sheet; season with salt and pepper. Using a fish spatula or your hands, place scallops on grill, flat side down. Grill, turning occasionally, until lightly charred and just cooked through, about 2 minutes per side. Serve scallops topped with Lemony Salsa Verde.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Mexican style green sauce originates from the Aztec Empire.

title: Instant Pot Mashed Potatoes

ingredients.raw: 4 lb. russet potatoes (about 8), peeled, cut into 2" pieces
4 1/2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 2 1/4 tsp. Morton kosher salt, divided
1 cup (1 stick) unsalted butter, cut into 1/2" pieces, plus more for serving if desired
1 tsp. freshly ground pepper, plus more

steps: Place 4 lb. russet potatoes (about 8), peeled, cut into 2" pieces, 4 garlic cloves, lightly smashed, 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1 tsp. Morton kosher salt, and 4 cups water in an Instant pot. Lock lid and set Instant Pot to cook at high pressure 12 minutes. (Instant Pot will take about 15–20 minutes to come to pressure.) Manually release (quick release) pressure, then remove lid. Drain potatoes.

Transfer potatoes back to warm Instant Pot insert. Using a potato masher, smash hot potatoes until mostly smooth. Add 1 cup (1 stick) unsalted butter, cut into 1/2" pieces, 1/2 cup whole milk, 1/4 cup sour cream, 1 tsp. freshly ground pepper, and remaining 2 1/2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1 1/4 tsp. Morton kosher salt and stir until butter is melted and sour cream is completely distributed throughout potatoes. If you’d like your potatoes smoother, continue mashing until you reach your desired consistency. Taste and season with more salt and pepper if needed.
Transfer potatoes to a medium bowl and top with pats of butter, thinly sliced chives, and more pepper, if desired.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Potatoes have been mashed in the Andes region since first domesticated around 8000 BCE.

title: Maple-Roasted Delicata Squash

ingredients.raw: 3 medium Delicata squash (about 3 pounds), halved lengthwise, seeded, and cut into 1/4"-thick slices
2 medium red onions, halved lengthwise and cut into 1/2" rings
Kosher salt, freshly ground black pepper
Kosher salt, freshly ground black pepper

steps: Arrange racks in the upper and lower rungs in the oven and preheat oven to 425°. Toss 3 medium Delicata squash (about 3 pounds), halved lengthwise, seeded, and cut into 1/4”-thick slices, 2 medium red onions, halved lengthwise and cut into 1/2” rings, 5 garlic cloves, peeled and smashed, 4 fresh thyme sprigs, 1/2 tsp. red-pepper flakes, 3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, and 2 Tbsp. maple syrup in a large bowl to combine. Season generously with kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper and toss again.

Spread squash mixture in a single layer onto 2 large rimmed baking sheets. Bake, tossing, rotating, and switching the pan positions halfway through cooking, until tender and browned, 25–30 minutes. Taste and season again with more salt and pepper if desired.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Modern American fall side dish.

title: Roasted Chicken Thighs with White Beans, Lemon, and Capers

ingredients.raw: 2 (15-ounce) cans white beans, drained and rinsed
1 large lemon, thinly sliced, seeds removed

steps: Position rack in upper third of oven and preheat to 425°F. Toss beans and capers in a 13x9" baking dish and spread out evenly on bottom of pan. Spread 1 tsp. mustard on skin of each chicken thigh and nestle, skin side up, into beans and capers. Arrange lemon slices under and around chicken and add enough water (about 1/3 cup) to come up sides of chicken by 1/2". Drizzle chicken with oil and season whole dish with salt and pepper.

Roast chicken, stirring and shaking dish halfway through, until skin is browned and an instant-read thermometer inserted into thickest part of chicken registers 165°F, about 35 minutes. If chicken skin starts to burn, move pan to a lower rack to finish cooking.
Transfer chicken, beans, lemon slices, and capers to a serving platter. Spoon some of the pan sauce around chicken and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Rustic Ratatouille

ingredients.raw: 4 small zucchini (about 1 pound), cut into 1-inch pieces
1 medium eggplant (about 1 pound), cut into 1-inch pieces
3 medium red bell peppers, cut into 1-inch pieces
2 cans (14 ounces each) chickpeas, rinsed and drained
8 plum tomatoes (about 1 pound), seeded and cut into 1-inch pieces
2 1/2 teaspoons sherry wine vinegar or balsamic vinegar

steps: Heat oven to 450°F. In a bowl, toss zucchini, eggplant, bell pepper and onion with thyme, rosemary, 3/4 teaspoon salt, black pepper, 2 tablespoons water and oil. Coat a rimmed sheet pan with cooking spray. Spread veggies in pan in a single layer; roast, stirring once, 25 minutes. In same bowl, combine chickpeas, tomatoes, garlic, tomato paste and remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt. Add to pan with veggies in a single layer; roast 10 to 12 minutes more. Toss veggies with vinegar; divide among 6 bowls; sprinkle with basil.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Traditionally, French ratatouille doesn't have chickpeas, but this recipe packs a bit more protein.

title: Sweet Bell Pepper and Onion Salad

ingredients.raw: 1 1/2 pounds orange or yellow bell peppers (about 4) or sweet orange peppers (about 6), thinly sliced into rings
1 small torpedo or red onion, thinly sliced into rings
2 tablespoons Sherry vinegar or red wine vinegar
1/4 cup coarsely chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley

steps: Toss bell peppers, onion, and vinegar in a large bowl; season with salt and black pepper.
Let sit until bell peppers are slightly softened, 10–20 minutes. Just before serving, toss herbs and oil with bell pepper mixture.

title: Teriyaki Salmon

ingredients.raw: 1 pound brussels sprouts, halved if large
1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, divided

steps: Position rack in middle of oven; heat oven to 450°F. In a bowl, combine teriyaki sauce, honey, vinegar, 1 teaspoon garlic, ginger and sesame oil. Place salmon in a shallow dish; sprinkle with 1 1/2 tablespoon teriyaki mixture; marinate 15 minutes. In a second bowl, toss brussels sprouts with 1 1/2 teaspoon garlic, 1/2 tablespoon canola oil, 1/4 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Coat a rimmed sheet pan with cooking spray. Spread brussels sprouts in pan in a single layer; roast until light brown, 5 minutes. In second bowl, toss mushrooms with remaining 1/2 tablespoon canola oil, 1 1/2 teaspoon garlic, 1/4 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Move brussels sprouts to center of pan; top with salmon; place mushrooms in pan around edges; roast, stirring mushrooms occasionally, until salmon is just cooked through, 8 to 10 minutes. Top salmon with remaining teriyaki mixture; serve over Brussels sprouts and mushrooms.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Teriyaki became a fish-cooking technique during the Edo period.

title: Tomato, Pickled Melon, and Burrata Salad

ingredients.raw: 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, plus more
1 pound Sharlyn or Galia melon, rind removed, sliced into thin rounds
12 ounces fresh burrata or mozzarella, torn

steps: Combine vinegar, kosher salt, 1/4 teaspoon pepper, and 2 tablespoons water in a large bowl; add melon and toss to coat. Let stand at room temperature at least 30 minutes.
Remove melon from pickling liquid and arrange on a platter with tomato and burrata. Drizzle with oil and some pickling liquid, top with basil, and season with sea salt and pepper.
Do ahead: Melon can be pickled 2 hours ahead. Cover and chill.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Burrata traditionally comes from the Puglia region in South Italy.

title: Fresno Chile Hot Sauce
steps: Cook 1/2 pound stemmed Fresno chiles (8–10) and 6 peeled garlic cloves in a large saucepan of boiling salted water until chiles turn bright red, about 2 minutes; drain. Blend chiles, garlic, and 3 tablespoons red wine vinegar in a blender until almost smooth; season with salt. Let cool.
Cooks' note: Do ahead: Hot sauce can be made 1 week ahead. Cover and chill.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Fresno chili was developed in Fresno and Clovis, California in the 1950s.

title: Mississippi Corn Pudding

ingredients.raw: 5 Tbsp. unsalted butter, melted and cooled slightly, plus more for greasing
1 lb. fresh corn kernels, cut from 4 cobs
1 cup butter cracker crumbs, such as Ritz

steps: Set a rack in the lower third of the oven. Preheat the oven to 350°F. Grease a 9x13" casserole dish with butter, making sure to get in all the corners and sides of the dish.
In a medium bowl, whisk together the eggs and sugar until well combined. Add the melted butter, milk, heavy cream, and sour cream and whisk to incorporate.
In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, cornmeal, salt, pepper, paprika, and baking soda.
Using a spatula, fold the wet ingredients, 1 cup at a time, into the dry ingredients until well combined.
Fold in the onion, celery, corn, and cheese.

Pour the batter into the prepared baking dish and sprinkle the cracker crumbs on top. Bake the pudding for 30 to 40 minutes, rotating halfway through, until lightly browned on top and the tip of a knife inserted in the center comes out clean.

Make Ahead: Corn casserole can be baked up to three days ahead of time. Let cool and refrigerate. Reheat, covered, in a 350°F oven until warmed through, about 15 minutes, remove cover and bake another 5 minutes to re-crisp topping.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Thanksgiving-related recipe; Thanksgiving is a very important holiday in the US and Canada.

title: Skillet Stuffing With Italian Sausage and Wild Mushrooms

ingredients.raw: 2 crusty white demi baguettes (about 10 1/2 ounces), cut into 3/4" cubes (about 8 cups cubes)
1/2 pound hot or sweet Italian sausage, casings removed
8 ounces wild mushrooms, cut into large pieces
1 1/2 ounces finely grated Parmesan or Pecorino (about 1/2 cup)

steps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Toast bread on a rimmed baking sheet until dry, about 10 minutes. Let cool. Reduce oven temperature to 375°F.

Meanwhile, heat 1 Tbsp. oil in a 12" cast-iron skillet over medium-high. Add sausage and cook, breaking into pieces with a spatula, until browned, about 7 minutes. Add onion, mushrooms, and sage and cook, stirring occasionally, until well browned, 8–10 minutes. Add wine and cook, stirring occasionally, until reduced by half. Let cool slightly.

Whisk eggs, broth, cheese, mustard, salt, and pepper in a large bowl. Add sausage mixture, reserving skillet, and bread and toss to combine. Let sit 5 minutes, toss again, then pack back into skillet.
Bake stuffing until lightly browned on top and cooked through, about 20 minutes.

Cooks' note: Demi baguettes are preferred for this recipe because they're wider than standard baguettes, yielding a better bread-to-crust ratio. If you can't find demi baguettes, you can use one white baguette that weighs about 10 1/2 ounces.

title: Maple-Pear Sheet Tart

ingredients.raw: 1 14- to 17-ounce box of puff pastry (preferably all-butter puff), defrosted according to package directions
2 large Anjou pears (about 1 1/4 pounds), skin on

steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F. Line a 13x18-inch baking sheet with parchment paper. In a small bowl, beat the egg with 1 tablespoon water.

If using a 14-ounce puff pastry package, roll the sheet to a 13-x18-inch rectangle on a floured surface. If using a 17-ounce puff pastry package, roll each sheet to a 9 1/2-x13-inch rectangle. Line up the two longer sides and overlap by 1 inch to form a 13-x18-inch rectangle. Brush egg wash in between to form a seam. Use a rolling pin to seal the seam.

Transfer the pastry to the parchment. Fold sides of pastry towards center to form a 1/2-inch border on all four sides. Lightly score the border by using a paring knife to make small shallow diagonal cuts. Prick the surface of the pastry inside the border with a fork. Refrigerate until ready to use.

Slice the pears in half lengthwise, and then cut lengthwise into 1/4-inch thick slices. Trim the seeds and core and toss the slices in the sugar. Arrange on the pastry and brush all exposed pastry (including the borders) with the egg wash.
Bake until the crust is puffed and golden brown, 45 to 50 minutes. Brush the fruit and pastry with the maple syrup. Let cool completely, and then slice into squares to serve.

title: Mulled Wine
description: Special equipment: A 4" square of cheesecloth; kitchen string

ingredients.raw: 4 cups dry red wine (from two 750-ml bottles)
1/2 cup kirsch or other cherry-flavored brandy

steps: Put cloves, peppercorns, and zest on cheesecloth, then tie closed to form a bag.
Combine wine, kirsch, sugar, cinnamon stick, vanilla bean, 1 1/2 cups water, and cheesecloth bag in a 4-qt. saucepan and bring to a boil, stirring.
Simmer 10 minutes. Serve warm, garnished with cinnamon sticks and orange wheels if using.

title: Roasted Sweet Potatoes With Spiced Maple Glaze

ingredients.raw: 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1 1/4 tsp. Morton kosher salt

steps: Preheat oven to 450°. Peel 2 lb. sweet potatoes (3–4 large), then slice crosswise 3/4"–1"-thick and cut into 3/4"–1" pieces. (You want them to be all about the same size so they cook evenly.) Transfer to a large bowl and add 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil and 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1 1/4 tsp. Morton kosher salt; toss to coat. Transfer sweet potatoes to a parchment-lined baking sheet, spreading out evenly; reserve bowl.
Roast sweet potatoes, tossing occasionally with a metal spatula, until browned and fork-tender, 20–25 minutes.
Meanwhile, whisk 3 Tbsp. pure maple syrup, 1 tsp. crushed red pepper flakes, 1 tsp. freshly ground black pepper, and 1 tsp. ground cinnamon in reserved bowl.
Transfer roasted sweet potatoes to bowl with spice mixture and toss to coat.

title: Butternut Squash Vegducken With Mushroom-Cranberry Stuffing

ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon plus 1 teaspoon kosher salt, plus more
16 ounces cremini mushrooms, coarsely chopped, divided
1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, divided, plus more
4 cups homemade or store-bought low-sodium vegetable broth

steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Toast pumpkin seeds on a rimmed baking sheet, tossing once, until fragrant and slightly darkened, 8–10 minutes. Transfer to a plate and let cool.

Increase oven temperature to 400°F. Line rimmed baking sheet with foil. Cut potato in half lengthwise. Using a medium-size, quick-release ice cream scoop or heavy spoon, scoop out flesh, leaving a small divot down the center. Reserve potato filling.

Place potato halves and parsnip in a large heatproof bowl; cover with plastic wrap. Microwave on high 5 minutes. Carefully check to see if vegetables are fork tender; if not, re-cover and microwave in 1-minute bursts until tender. (Alternatively, roast potato halves and parsnip on a rimmed baking sheet in a 400°F oven until fork-tender, about 50 minutes for parsnip and 30 minutes for potatoes. Let cool slightly.)
Meanwhile, cut squash in half lengthwise, remove seeds, and discard. Scoop out flesh, leaving a divot deep enough to fit potato inside and at least a 1/2" border on all sides. Reserve squash filling.
Using a fork, pierce insides of squash and potato halves, then pierce parsnip all over.

Pulse garlic and thyme in a food processor, scraping down sides as necessary. Add paprika, 1/4 cup oil, and 1 Tbsp. kosher salt and continue to pulse until a thick paste forms, about 1 minute. Transfer to a small bowl.

Working in batches, pulse squash and potato filling in food processor until coarsely chopped, about 30 seconds. Transfer to a large bowl. Pulse 4 oz. mushrooms in food processor until coarsely chopped, about 30 seconds. Transfer to same bowl and stir to combine.

Heat 1 Tbsp. garlic-oil mixture in a large nonstick skillet over medium until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Add vegetable purée and cook, stirring occasionally, until mixture is browned and moisture releases, about 12 minutes. Return to bowl and let cool.
Add eggs, Parmesan, breadcrumbs, cranberries, 3 Tbsp. parsley, 1/4 tsp. kosher salt, 1/4 tsp. pepper, and 1/4 cup pumpkin seeds to bowl and mix to combine.

Place squash halves, cut side up, on prepared baking sheet. Using a pastry brush, coat inside with garlic-oil mixture. Using the back of a spoon, press 1 cup vegetable mixture into each half until interior is fully coated.

Nestle potato halves, cut side up, inside squash halves. Brush with garlic-oil mixture. Using the back of a spoon, press 6 Tbsp. vegetable mixture into each half until interior is fully coated. Discard remaining vegetable mixture.
Trim parsnip to fit inside 1 potato half. Brush parsnip with garlic-oil mixture and place inside.

Cut 3 (18") lengths of kitchen twine. Slip twine under 1 squash half, then top with second squash half so cut sides face each other, and press down to seal. Tightly tie twine around squash to secure. Brush top with garlic-oil mixture, reserving remaining mixture, and season with 1/2 tsp. kosher salt. Wrap squash tightly in foil and place in center of baking sheet. Using 2 loaf pans or small metal bowls turned upside down, keep squash secure on baking sheet.
Bake vegducken, carefully flipping halfway through, until squash is tender, 1 hour–1 hour, 20 minutes. Let rest 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, heat 1 Tbsp. reserved garlic-oil mixture in a medium pot over medium-low until beginning to brown and smells fragrant, about 30 seconds. Cook shallot, bay leaves, and remaining 12 oz. mushrooms, stirring occasionally, until mushrooms are tender and beginning to brown, about 5 minutes. Add broth, bring to a simmer, and cook 30 minutes.

Strain mushroom mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a large bowl; wipe out pot. Cook flour and remaining 2 Tbsp. oil in pot over medium heat, stirring constantly, until nutty brown and thickened, about 8 minutes.
Add wine, bring to a simmer, and cook 3 minutes. Add mushroom broth, 1 Tbsp. parsley, 1/4 tsp. kosher salt, and 1/4 tsp. pepper, and return to a simmer. Season to taste.

Place vegducken on a cutting board and cut into 1" slices with a serrated knife, transferring to serving plates as you go. Spoon gravy over. Top with remaining 1/4 cup pepitas and 2 Tbsp. parsley. Season with sea salt and serve.

Cooks' note: The sizes of the squash, sweet potato, and parsnip can vary a bit from the lengths specified; the key is that they fit/nestle into one another. When possible, choose squash that has a neck and bulb and sweet potato that are as uniform in width as possible. If necessary, use 1 medium and 1 small sweet potato and trim, then stagger to fit together into the squash.

title: Torta Pasqualina
description: Special equipment: A 10"-diameter tart pan with a removable bottom

ingredients.raw: 1 1/2 cups (3 sticks) unsalted butter, cut into pieces, chilled in freezer (dough)
3 1/2 lb. Swiss chard (about 5 bunches), ribs and stems removed (filling and assembly)
3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil (filling and assembly)
2 medium onions, finely chopped (filling and assembly)
1 1/2 cups whole-milk fresh ricotta, preferably box-drained, patted dry (filling and assembly)
4 oz. Parmesan, coarsely grated (filling and assembly)
1 large garlic clove, finely grated (filling and assembly)
2 tsp. finely grated lemon zest (filling and assembly)
1/4 tsp. freshly grated nutmeg (filling and assembly)
2 tsp. kosher salt, plus more (filling and assembly)
1 1/2 tsp. freshly ground black pepper, plus more (filling and assembly)
1/2 cup plus 1 Tbsp. ice water (from the steps)

steps: Dough: Pulse flour, sugar, and salt in a food processor to combine. Add butter and process until largest pieces of butter are pea-size. Drizzle in 1/2 cup ice water and pulse until a few shaggy pieces of dough form.

Transfer dough (get all the dry bits) to a work surface. Drizzle 1 Tbsp. ice water over; knead to just barely bring dough together. Divide in half. Place a half on a piece of plastic wrap. Using plastic and your hands, form dough into a 3/4"-thick disk and tightly wrap. Repeat with remaining dough. Chill at least 2 hours.

Filing and assembly: Working in batches, cook Swiss chard in a large pot of boiling water until bright green and slightly softened, about 2 minutes. Using tongs, transfer to an ice bath to stop the cooking. Swish to cool, then remove greens and squeeze out as much excess liquid as possible. Transfer greens to a cutting board and finely chop (you should have about 4 cups).
Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium. Cook onions, stirring occasionally, until very soft and golden but not browned, 8–10 minutes. Remove from heat and mix in greens. Let cool.

Using a fork, whisk 4 eggs in a large bowl to blend. Add ricotta, Parmesan, and Swiss chard mixture and mix to combine. Add garlic, lemon zest, nutmeg, 2 tsp. salt, and 1 1/2 tsp. pepper. Taste and adjust seasoning, if needed.

Let dough sit at room temperature 5 minutes to soften. Roll out 1 disk of dough on a lightly floured surface to a 12" round about 1/8" thick. Transfer to a parchment-lined rimmed baking sheet. Roll out remaining disk of dough and carefully transfer to tart pan. Lift up edges and allow dough to slump down into pan. Press dough firmly into sides and bottom of pan. Trim, leaving about a 1/2" overhang. Beat 1 egg in a small bowl to blend and brush edges of dough.

Scrape filling into pan, creating a mound in the center. Using an offset spatula, evenly spread filling over bottom, smoothing surface. Use a spoon to create 5 divots in filling and crack an egg into each. Season eggs with a bit of salt. Arrange remaining round of dough over filling. Trim edges of top round, leaving 1/2" overhang. Fold edge of bottom crust up and over top, then press edges together to seal. Crimp and brush top of dough with remaining beaten egg; sprinkle with sugar. Transfer pie to a foil-lined rimmed baking sheet and chill in freezer 10 minutes.
Preheat oven to 375°F. Bake pie until crust is deep golden brown, 65–75 minutes. Transfer pan to a wire rack and let pie cool in pan at least 30 minutes before serving.
Do ahead: Dough can be made 5 days ahead. Keep chilled, or freeze up to 1 month. Pie can be baked 1 day ahead. Let cool; cover and chill.
